Subject: Request: subprocessor origin & KMS keyflow for DPA review

Hi Ben —

As part of our data processing review for the upcoming contract amendment, we need a concise mapping of which subprocessors handle customer data originating in the EU, plus a diagram of key management flows (KMS/HSM) showing where keys are generated, stored, and whether any secrets cross borders. Our GC and security team want to confirm there are no offshored key-material transfers that would impact our data residency requirements.

Would you be able to provide:
- A CSV or table listing each subprocessor, the country of processing, and the specific data path (ingest, telemetry, logs, backups)
- A KMS/keyflow diagram (high level) showing key generation, escrow (if any), and where key-encrypted artifacts reside
- Any temporary exceptions or planned migrations in the next 90 days that could affect EU-origin data

I've attached the DPA scope page (Acme_DPA_Scope.pdf) to highlight the clauses we're focusing on. Ideally we need this by EOD Tuesday so our procurement team can proceed.

Thanks,

Hi Jane / Acme team —

Thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. Apologies for the tight turnaround; attached are the deliverables you requested. High-level summary below.

1) Subprocessor origin mapping: attached CSV (redwood_subprocessors_mapping_v1.csv) lists all subprocessors that may touch customer-origin payloads. Columns include: processor name, role (ingest/storage/telemetry/cdn/backup), primary country-of-processing, persistence, and SOC2/KMS attestations (where applicable). Short callouts:
- EdgeCacheCo (CDN) — ephemeral edge caching in EU regions; logs are transient and retained for 48 hours by default; backups do not leave eu-central-1 for EU tenants.
- TelemetryInc — aggregated metrics are exported to our centralized analytics pipeline in us-west-2 (pseudonymized); we flagged this as a potential scope item per your DPA language.

2) KMS/keyflow diagram: attached (kms_keyflow_sketch.png) is a 1-page diagram showing key lifecycle for EU tenants:
- DEK (data encryption keys) are generated per-tenant in eu-central-1 KMS; DEKs are wrapped by a Root Key that is stored in a customer-dedicated HSM cluster (on-prem equivalent) for enterprise Private deployments, or in a Redwood-managed EU HSM for hosted customers.
- Key wrapping/unwrapping occurs inside eu-central-1 for EU tenants. No unwrapped key material leaves the region.
- For telemetry aggregation that ships to us-west-2, telemetry payloads are pseudonymized and encrypted at rest; keys are not exported — only encrypted artifacts are transferred.

3) Planned changes / exceptions:
- We're planning a telemetry processing pipeline migration in Q4 that will introduce an optional EU-only telemetry shard; that will reduce cross-border movement. No immediate export changes in the next 90 days.

Next steps:
- If Acme would like a higher-fidelity diagram or an in-person tech-call, we can schedule a 30-minute session with our security engineering lead.
- If the audit requires an attestation copy for our EU HSM provider, Laura can coordinate procurement/contract documents.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_mapping_v1.csv; kms_keyflow_sketch.png
